answer.generated: To determine the number of processors with the highest speedup under the given conditions, we need to balance the reduction in execution time due to parallelization against the increase in communication costs. Let \( n \) represent the number of processors. The speedup \( S(n) \) can be expressed as the ratio of the original execution time \( T_0 \) to the new execution time \( T(n) \), where \( T(n) = T_0 - \frac{P}{100}T_0 + \frac{0.5n}{100}T_0 \). Simplifying, we get \( T(n) = T_0(1 - \frac{P}{100} + \frac{0.5n}{100}) \). Therefore, the speedup \( S(n) = \frac{T_0}{T(n)} = \frac{1}{1 - \frac{P}{100} + \frac{0.5n}{100}} \). The maximum speedup occurs when the derivative of \( S(n) \) with respect to \( n \) equals zero, indicating the point at which the benefits of adding more processors are offset by the increasing communication overhead.
